metadata.title: Client Archetypes & Sample Programs
metadata.purpose: Reference profiles showing Claude exactly what a finished TRAIN program looks like for different client types. These are not real clients — they are programming templates. Claude uses these as blueprints when generating personalized programs.
metadata.how_to_use: When generating a new client program, identify which archetype(s) the client most closely matches. Use that archetype's program structure as the foundation, then personalize using the client's actual onboarding data.
metadata.output_note: Each real client receives their own generated file: program_[clientname].html — never overwrite another client's file.

archetypes.name: The Returning Mom
archetypes.description: Was active before kids, took 2-5 years off, wants to feel like herself again. Motivated but time-constrained. High emotional investment in her body changing.

programming_approach.starting_volume: Conservative — 60% of standard. Build habits first.
programming_approach.tone: Warm, encouraging, celebrate every win. Frame sessions around energy and feeling, not aesthetics.

exercises.name: Goblet Squat
exercises.cue: Chest tall, sit into your hips

exercises.name: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
exercises.cue: Push hips back, soft knee, feel the hamstring load

exercises.name: Dumbbell Row (single arm)
exercises.cue: Drive elbow to hip, not ceiling

exercises.name: Dumbbell Shoulder Press
exercises.cue: Core braced, don't arch the lower back

exercises.name: Glute Bridge
exercises.cue: Squeeze hard at top, hold 1 second

exercises.name: Dead Bug
exercises.cue: Lower back stays pressed to floor the entire time

exercises.name: Reverse Lunge
exercises.cue: Step back, lower straight down

exercises.name: Dumbbell Hip Thrust
exercises.cue: Drive through heels, full glute squeeze at top

exercises.name: Dumbbell Chest Press
exercises.cue: Lower to chest, press up and slightly in

exercises.name: Band Pull-Apart
exercises.cue: Pinch shoulder blades together at end

exercises.name: Lateral Band Walk
exercises.cue: Stay low, toes forward, feel the outer hip

exercises.name: Pallof Press
exercises.cue: Press out, hold 1 second, resist rotation

mesocycle_progression.week_2: Add 1 set to primary compound movements. RPE climbs to 7-8.
mesocycle_progression.week_3: Add weight where RIR allows. RPE 8. Introduce 1 superset pairing.
mesocycle_progression.week_4: Deload — drop to 2 sets, reduce load 40%, same movements.
mesocycle_progression.mesocycle_2: Increase baseline. Add 1 exercise per session. Consider upper/lower split if schedule allows.

archetypes.kim_program_note: You showed up. That's the hardest part — and you did it. This program is built around your life, not against it. Three days is enough to change everything when you're consistent. Let's go.

archetypes.name: The Returning Athlete
archetypes.description: Played sports in college or high school, hasn't trained seriously in years. High body awareness, competitive mindset, needs to be reigned in early to prevent injury from going too hard too fast.

programming_approach.starting_volume: 75% of target — hold them back early, let them earn the volume
programming_approach.intensity: RPE 7 weeks 1-2, RPE 8 weeks 3-4. They will want to go harder — hold the line.
programming_approach.tone: Data-driven. Give them numbers to chase. PRs, weekly load targets, performance metrics.

exercises.name: Face Pull
exercises.cue: Rotator cuff health — never skip this

exercises.name: Barbell Back Squat
exercises.note: Heel elevation if ankle restriction — earn the depth over weeks

exercises.name: Bulgarian Split Squat
exercises.cue: Weaker leg first — match reps exactly

mesocycle_progression.week_2: Add 5 lbs to all compound movements where RPE allows. RPE 8.
mesocycle_progression.week_3: Add 1 set to primary compounds. RPE 8-9. This is the hardest week.
mesocycle_progression.mesocycle_2: Switch to weekly undulating — rotate hypertrophy, strength, and volume weeks.

archetypes.kim_program_note: Your body remembers more than you think. Muscle memory is real — but we build back smart, not fast. Trust the process for 4 weeks and your numbers will surprise you.

archetypes.name: The Complete Beginner
archetypes.description: Little to no training history. May be nervous or intimidated. Needs wins early, movement pattern education, and a program that feels achievable.

programming_approach.starting_volume: Minimum effective volume — 2 sets only. Add sets in week 3.
programming_approach.intensity: RPE 5-6 weeks 1-2. They need to feel capable, not destroyed.
programming_approach.tone: Patient, educational, celebrate every single session. Explain everything. No assumed knowledge.
programming_approach.special_note: Include detailed mind-muscle cues on every exercise. Tempo is introduced week 3 only.

session_A.label: Full Body — Session A
session_A.warm_up: Full body protocol — 10 min (take extra time here)

exercises.name: Bodyweight Squat
exercises.cue: Feet shoulder width, sit back like there's a chair behind you, chest stays up

exercises.name: Glute Bridge
exercises.cue: Drive through your heels. Squeeze your glutes at the top — hold for 1 full second

exercises.name: Dumbbell Row (light)
exercises.cue: Pull your elbow toward your hip. Think about squeezing the muscle between your shoulder blades

exercises.name: Push-Up (on knees if needed)
exercises.cue: Body in a straight line. Lower your chest to the floor, push back up

exercises.name: Dead Bug
exercises.cue: Lower back must stay flat on the floor the whole time. This is the only rule.

mesocycle_progression.week_2: Same exercises, aim for top of rep range. Add bodyweight awareness.
mesocycle_progression.week_3: Add 1 set to all exercises. Introduce light dumbbells where bodyweight was used. Introduce tempo.
mesocycle_progression.week_4: Deload — back to 2 sets, lighter load. Celebrate the full month.
mesocycle_progression.mesocycle_2: Introduce dumbbell loading across all movements. Add 1 exercise per session.

archetypes.kim_program_note: Starting is the hardest rep you'll ever do — and you already did it. Everything from here is momentum. You don't need to be perfect. You just need to show up three times a week and follow the plan. That's it. Let's go.

archetypes.name: The Intermediate Female — Body Recomp
archetypes.description: 1-3 years of training, consistent but plateaued. Wants to lose fat and gain muscle simultaneously. Needs more stimulus variety and progressive overload structure she hasn't had.

programming_approach.periodization: Daily Undulating Periodization — different rep ranges each session
programming_approach.starting_volume: Full target volume — she can handle it
programming_approach.tone: Balanced — give her data and feeling. She responds to both. Reference her why when pushing.

exercises.name: Barbell Hip Thrust
exercises.cue: This is your strength movement — load it heavy

mesocycle_progression.week_2: Add weight where RIR 2+ consistently. RPE climbs to 8.
mesocycle_progression.week_3: Add 1 set to primary compounds. RPE 8-9. Hardest week.
mesocycle_progression.mesocycle_2: Shift DUP rotation — add volume week, reduce strength week frequency.

archetypes.kim_program_note: You've been consistent — now let's make the program match your capacity. This structure is going to feel different from what you've been doing. That difference is the point. Your body needed a new signal. This is it.

archetypes.name: The Autoimmune Client
archetypes.description: Managing a chronic condition (fibromyalgia, lupus, rheumatoid arthritis, MS, Hashimoto's, etc.). Energy is variable. Flare days are real. Needs a flexible, compassionate program that adapts to how she feels.

programming_approach.periodization: Linear conservative — deload every 3 weeks not 4
programming_approach.starting_volume: 60% of minimum effective volume. Build trust with the body first.
programming_approach.intensity: RPE 5-7 MAX. Never push to failure. Never.
programming_approach.energy_check_in: Always check energy (1-10) before session. Scale accordingly.
programming_approach.tone: Gentle, non-pressuring. Honor the body. Celebrate showing up — not performance.

session_scaling.energy_1_to_4: Rest or gentle walk only. No training.
session_scaling.energy_5_to_6: Half session — 2-3 exercises only, RPE 5, focus on feel-good movement

session_A.label: Full Body — Energy Permitting

exercises.name: Goblet Squat (light)
exercises.cue: Move with intention. Feel each muscle. No rushing.

session_A.cooldown: Active recovery protocol — 15 min (extended for this client)

mesocycle_progression.week_2: Only progress if energy has been consistently 7+. If not — maintain.
mesocycle_progression.week_3: Deload regardless of how good she feels.
mesocycle_progression.mesocycle_2: Assess. If energy patterns have improved, consider adding 1 exercise. Never rush volume.

archetypes.kim_program_note: Your body is not your enemy — it's communicating. This program is built to listen. Some days we train hard. Some days we move gently. Some days we rest. All three are the right answer. I'm here for every version of you.

archetypes.name: The Post-Injury Client
archetypes.description: Recovering from or working around a specific injury (knee, shoulder, lower back, hip). Has clearance to train but needs full modification of affected area.

programming_approach.principle: Never remove all training — always find what CAN be done. Injury is not an excuse to stop — it's a reason to get smarter.
programming_approach.cross_reference: injury_navigation.json — apply all contraindications and substitutions for the specific injury
programming_approach.volume: Reduce affected area volume by 50%. Maintain or increase volume for unaffected areas.
programming_approach.tone: Empowering. Redirect focus to what the body CAN do. Reframe injury as information.

session_A.label: Full Body — Lower Back Modified
session_A.warm_up: Lower body protocol modified — Cat-Cow, Bird Dog, Glute Bridge, Hip Circle (no loaded movements)

exercises.name: Barbell Hip Thrust
exercises.note: Safe hip hinge — minimal spinal compression

exercises.name: Dead Bug
exercises.note: Core stability is the priority for lower back clients

session_A.cooldown: Lower body cooldown with extra hip flexor and child's pose emphasis — 10 min

archetypes.kim_program_note: Your body is communicating — not betraying you. We adjust, we don't abandon. There is always a way to train. Let's find yours.

archetypes.name: The Busy Professional
archetypes.description: High achiever, inconsistent schedule, travels frequently. Wants results but can only commit to 2-3 short sessions. Needs maximum efficiency — no fluff.

programming_approach.split: Full Body 3x/week — superset heavy for time efficiency
programming_approach.periodization: Linear 4-week — deload every 4 weeks or during heavy travel weeks
programming_approach.volume: Lower per session, higher density — supersets throughout
programming_approach.intensity: RPE 7-8 — short on time doesn't mean easy
programming_approach.session_structure: Every exercise paired in superset. Zero wasted time. 30 min is enough.
programming_approach.travel_protocol: Bodyweight session available for hotel or travel weeks — same movements, zero equipment

session_A.label: Full Body — 30 Min Maximum
session_A.structure_note: All exercises in superset pairs — minimal rest between pairs

travel_session.label: Hotel / No Equipment Session
travel_session.note: Same session quality, zero equipment. Consistency over conditions.

archetypes.kim_program_note: 30 minutes of focused, intentional work beats 90 minutes of distracted training every time. You're not short on time — you're short on wasted movement. This program has none.

archetypes.name: The Advanced Female — Performance
archetypes.description: 3+ years of consistent training, strong movement literacy, wants to push performance. Needs periodization, heavy compound work, and a program that matches her capacity.

programming_approach.split: Push/Pull/Legs — 5 days with active recovery day 6
programming_approach.starting_volume: Upper range — she can handle it and needs it
programming_approach.tone: Direct, data-focused, performance-framed. Give her PRs to chase.

mesocycle_progression.week_2: Add weight on all compounds where RPE allows. RPE 8-9.
mesocycle_progression.week_3: Add 1 set to primary compounds. RPE 9 on primary lifts. Hardest week.
mesocycle_progression.mesocycle_2: Intensification block — reduce volume, increase load. 4-6 rep primary work.

archetypes.kim_program_note: You've put in the time. Now let's see what you're actually made of. This program is going to challenge you in ways your current training hasn't. That's exactly the point. Trust the structure. Log everything. Let's set some PRs.

how_claude_uses_archetypes.step_2: Identify primary archetype match — which profile is closest?
how_claude_uses_archetypes.step_3: Note any secondary archetype overlaps (e.g. Returning Mom with injury = ARCH-01 + ARCH-06)
how_claude_uses_archetypes.step_4: Use matched archetype's programming structure as the template
how_claude_uses_archetypes.step_5: Replace archetype's sample exercises with personalized selections from exercise libraries based on client's actual goal, equipment, and limitations
how_claude_uses_archetypes.step_6: Apply client's exact onboarding data — their identity statement, vision, and motivation style to the program notes
how_claude_uses_archetypes.step_7: Generate output as program_[clientname].html — never overwrite another client's file
